subject: Information Theory
title: Mutual Information
description: A quick win: understand Mutual Information.

hook.text: The word 'doctor' makes 'hospital' more likely. Mutual information measures how much one word reveals about another.

buildup.text: Mutual information quantifies shared information between two variables. I(X;Y) = H(X) - H(X|Y).

discovery.text: High mutual information means knowing one word strongly predicts the other. It captures semantic association.

twist.text: Unlike correlation, mutual information captures nonlinear relationships. It detects associations linear measures miss.

climax.text: NLP uses mutual information for feature selection, word association, and topic modeling across languages.

punchline.text: How much does one word reveal about another? Exactly that much.

quiz.question: What does mutual information measure?
options: How much knowing one variable reduces uncertainty about another
